question: The number of white rooks used in chess is _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Two**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In a standard game of chess, each player starts with two rooks.
 
• The rooks are placed at the corners of the chessboard.
 
• The white rooks are initially placed on the squares a1 and h1.
 
• Rooks move horizontally or vertically any number of squares without jumping over other pieces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chessboard Setup:**

 
 
• A standard chessboard consists of 64 squares arranged in an 8x8 grid.
 
• Each player starts with 16 pieces: 1 king, 1 queen, 2 rooks, 2 knights, 2 bishops, and 8 pawns.
 
 
 
• **Rook Movement:**
 
 
• The rook can move horizontally or vertically through any number of unoccupied squares.
 
• It cannot jump over other pieces.
 
• The rook is a powerful piece, especially in the endgame when it can control open files and ranks.
 
 
 
• **Chess Strategies Involving Rooks:**
 
 
• Rooks are most effective when placed on open files or ranks where they can exert their power over a larger area of the board.
 
• Doubling rooks on a file (placing them one behind the other) increases their power and control.
 
• The rook and king work together effectively in the endgame to checkmate the opponent's king.
